---
title: "How do sample means vary across repeated resampling?"
---

## Question

How do sample means vary across repeated resampling?

## Work through it

Choose a numeric sample and a resample size; bootstrap from observed values with replacement; compare the distribution of resampled means with the original mean.

## Worked example: iris

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("iris")
means <- ru_apply("sampling_distribution", data=d,
                  x="Sepal.Length", n=30, reps=500, seed=42)
stopifnot(length(means)==500,all(is.finite(means)))
```

The histogram displays an empirical bootstrap distribution for 30-draw means from the recorded sepal lengths. It describes resampling from this dataset, not a guaranteed sampling distribution for all plants.

## Adapt to another question

```r
ru_apply("sampling_distribution", data=your_data, x="numeric_column", n=30, reps=500, seed=42)
```

If a question specifies a known probabilistic population model, simulate from that model instead of bootstrapping observed values.

Check the input conditions with `ru_plan("sampling_distribution")` before treating a calculation as an inference.
